title: Scheduled telemetry prefetch and rotation-aware alert throttler
author: Amina Velasquez
description: Adds a lightweight scheduled telemetry prefetch daemon and a rotation-aware alert throttler to reduce on-call noise during shift boundaries and warm up commonly-accessed metric slices for faster triage. Motivation: frequent handoffs see spike-driven alert storms and late-query latency when dashboards/queries are cold; this PR introduces a policy-driven prefetch scheduler that warms key telemetry windows ahead of shift boundaries and an alert throttling policy that defers non-critical noisy alerts during controlled handoff windows. Implementation includes a pluggable schedule config, per-rotation target lists, a backoff-safe fetch queue, and an alert throttler with reasons/annotations for observability. The change is backward compatible and default-disabled via flags; rollout plan is staged: opt-in config, dogfood in SRE rotation for 2 weeks, enable with conservative windows, then widen. Includes unit tests, integration test harness that simulates rotation boundaries, docs for operators, and a migration note for existing alert suppression rules. Checklist: 1) Feature flag gating present; 2) Add config to staging manifests; 3) Run load test with prefetch enabled; 4) Confirm no regressions on consumer dashboards; 5) Post-rollout telemetry baseline established. Related: ENG-3421 for scheduling policy design, SRE-772 for oncall noise analysis.
